whoRunsThis.refusal: Every one of those systems refuses to buy any coin launched through this platform, by mint address and by ticker, on every chain they trade. The refusal is code, not a promise: src/lib/ownTokens.ts reads config/own-tokens.json and every entry path asks it before a buy. A list that cannot be read refuses every entry (fail closed). wallets.label: keeper data key
wallets.description: The keeper signs readings and cranks; LaunchLab's recorded creator is the program's fee PDA. As an attester (quorum 1 at launch) it signs settled readings; as fee payer it sends cranks, claims and health checks. It cannot change a rule, burn more than the rule says, or withdraw from any fee PDA (see the Powers Register).

Holder: a dedicated encrypted key held by the operator; it cannot be transferred to the Squads vault (Raydium derives the platform id from the admin key) — disclosed as an untimelocked power (Powers Register, 'Powers outside the program'). Any change shows on this page within one cycle; initialize_token pins cpConfigId, platformCpCreator and the LP scales, and the launch gate re-reads them immediately before each create.

limitations.text: Quorum 1 at launch: the operator's keeper key is the only attester. The program verifies signatures and the quorum, not the reading itself. A second, independent attester is required before strangers launch.

Switchboard Technology Labs ended all oracle services on 2026-09-25. The Switchboard attester in this code is built against the pinned SDK and cannot run live. The planned replacements — a Reclaim zkTLS proof of the source response posted by a relayer key, and/or a second human operator running the reader on another machine — are not live. One operator attester is configured; no independent second attester is live, and who runs one and when is an open owner decision.

Kalshi is not a settlement input. Its Developer Agreement v1.1 limits API use to a member's own trading and forbids caching or sharing API data with third parties without written authorization; its Data Terms of Use forbid using Kalshi Data to create, settle or support products without written consent. The Kalshi adapter remains in the code as discovery-only behind BURNTICKER_KALSHI_ENABLED (default off) and the launch preflight refuses any Kalshi rule regardless of the flag. With the flag off the keeper does not read Kalshi at all, not even for a coin already registered with a Kalshi rule: such a coin is held (no readings, nothing burned) with a venue-disabled alert (owner decision 2026-10-10, after the ChatGPT/Codex review's C1). No mainnet Kalshi coin exists; devnet rehearsal coins may stall. Coins settle on first-party primaries with an independent cross-read, or on an on-chain Polymarket payout; Polymarket's Gamma API is used for discovery only and no prices, odds or volumes are displayed (its terms restrict market-data distribution).

One-shot markets are allowed: a coin bound to a single market resolves once, on that market's close. What happens after is its rule's onEnd schedule, not a fixed supply: a YES at 100% drains the burn pool one unit a day under the spend cap; any other end winds the pool down over 28 days (enough daily units to spend at least 99%), then the coin retires, and a retired coin's pool is swept again when new fees pass the sweep threshold, at most once a week. The token page shows the schedule.

Pre-audit cap: each burn pool spends from at most 25 SOL per burn day; SOL above the cap stays in the fee PDA until the next day. In the program it is PlatformConfig's cap with a sunset of at most 365 days, raisable only through a 48 h public timelock; the keeper models the same cap. Until the program is deployed only the keeper enforces it.

The devnet rehearsal ran on 2026-10-10: $DEFICIT launched under a devnet platform config, readings attested, two buy-back burns cranked by the program (2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07; the 2026-10-08 row in docs/burnkeeper/evidence/devnet-2026-10-10/burns.json is planned, not executed — deferred by TwapDeviation when the keeper was stopped, with no burn and no signature — and is not counted); then the pair_curve rehearsal (two pairs: one graduated to two Raydium pools, one voided and sold back). Records: docs/burnkeeper/devnet-run.md, docs/burnkeeper/devnet-run-log-2026-10-10.md, docs/burnkeeper/devnet-paircurve-run-log-2026-10-10.md and docs/burnkeeper/evidence/ (every signature checked against devnet by scripts/ops/verify-evidence-signatures.mjs). The mainnet rehearsal coin is a separate step and is not done (see Rehearsal coins).

burn_receipts (AuQjoSgq7upmyPBv2itwy2TSZ1VjoVipyy4z9wd7zhMM) and pair_curve (2jQotwSG8WKNYr5pccxuVmNa314qcnnwmrhqbuakELkN) are deployed on devnet, upgrade authority held by a 2-of-3 Squads vault; their bytes match a build of this repository (docs/burnticker/VERIFIED-BUILD.md). Neither is deployed on mainnet. Pages read the devnet programs where an RPC is configured; the launch wizard refuses mainnet and answers ready: false.

Raydium LaunchLab's PlatformConfig admin has no on-chain timelock (LaunchLab has none) and cannot be moved to the Squads vault after creation (the platform id is derived from the admin key). It is a dedicated encrypted key held by the operator, disclosed as an untimelocked power; the mitigations are the pins taken at initialize_token, the pre-create re-check and the live-vs-designed comparison on this page, not a lock.
The operator's contact address is contact@burnticker.com (security reports: security@burnticker.com).

The public repository is live: https://github.com/rfzfhn67yk-netizen/burnticker, carved out of the private monorepo by scripts/ops/publish-public-repo.sh and config/public-repo.allowlist. A GitHub organisation for it is an owner step (docs/burnticker/TODO-OWNER.md).

No company stands behind the platform yet: it is operated by one independent individual, whose identity is held privately, described on /burnticker/operator. An LLC is an open owner decision (TODO_ENTITY).

The two pair_curve reviews (2026-10-10) found High-severity issues (close_pair could strand the burn-pool registration, a pre-funded pool vault or a pre-created token account could block graduation or init_pair, an executable developer wallet could freeze trades). All findings are fixed or accepted in writing (docs/burn-receipts/CHANGELOG.md, code fa8627a4), the reviewers' exploit tests now assert each attack fails, and the fixed program was re-rehearsed on devnet (docs/burnkeeper/devnet-paircurve-run-log-2026-10-10.md §R2). An independent re-check confirmed the fixes and found five residuals (a post-deadline curve-sell race, a stuck-side lock without an AmmConfig signal, a close blocked by an executable developer wallet, the upgrade script's hash check, an unsynced WSOL donation); all fixed in fcda14eb and spot-checked on devnet (§R3). Not yet done: a review of the round-2 code. Pair launches stay off for mainnet (BURNTICKER_PAIR_CURVE_ENABLED) until it is done.

The mainnet burn_receipts and pair_curve builds compile the operator treasury 8cwwy895BENMJTueXfQovWD4mvuoJ4kgyR52UMrqSbo5 (the owner's hardware wallet, also the LaunchLab platform fee wallet) and the Burnticker LaunchLab platform 94x5qDDJP4UCkeMWppnmvqTmMgo971h3d6MDRnjEfYy9 (owner, 2026-10-11; docs/burnticker/VERIFIED-BUILD.md). claim_lock_fees pays the operator's 20 % there; initialize_token accepts only that platform.

policies.text: On X: nothing is deleted. A mistake is corrected in-thread, with the receipt (the transaction and the recomputation) attached.
No Telegram or Discord: Burnticker and $DEFICIT communicate only through @burnticker / @USA_DEFICIT on X and the public repository. Any channel claiming otherwise is not ours.
Failure definition: if any coin on this platform trades at any price, nothing changes — no relaunch, no v2, no rebrand, no change to a rule. The rule runs and the receipts post.

No paid promotion, no influencer payments, no referral kickbacks. No price talk and no countdowns: no price, market cap or odds for any Burnticker coin; another coin's market cap may be a rule input, shown only as the rule sentence (Burn Derby's flippening; derby admission refuses a Burnticker coin as an input).
The platform never buys any coin, including its own. Burn pools buy only inside crank_buyback, by the rule, and burn what they receive. The operator's trading bots refuse platform coins.
Nothing on any surface is described as coming later. If it is not built, this page lists it as not built, with its status.
Creators receive no cash from fees; the creator-fee slot pays the burn pool, 100%. Zero team allocation on any coin. Seed deposits to a burn pool are gifts with no claim.

LP locked forever; its fees fund the burn (80% burned, 20% operator, fixed in code). At graduation 100 % of every coin's LP is locked with Raydium's LP lock and can never be withdrawn; the Fee Key NFT is owned by the burn_receipts PDA ["fee_keys"], not a person. Anyone can call claim_lock_fees: the SOL side goes 80 % to the coin's burn pool and 20 % to the operator treasury (the Squads vault), the coin side is burned; the split is compiled into the program (LOCK_FEE_BURN_BPS 8000, LOCK_FEE_OPERATOR_BPS 2000), with no admin key or config field. The operator earns 20 % of post-graduation LP fees: 4.2 bps of every swap after graduation, next to 16.8 bps to the burn pool. Owner decision 2026-10-10 (decisions.md), replacing the 2026-10-09 burned-LP policy.
The platform does not reply to or amplify return-marketing. A creator who markets returns using our pages loses the embed, not the rule.
Rules, readings and receipts are append-only. Corrections are new entries that name what they correct; the incident log and this decision log are never edited after the fact.
The memecoin disclaimer and the event-contract disclosure sit on every surface that describes the mechanic.
